Subject: Storage Sherpa: idempotency, sync contracts & partner playbook — invite

Hi all,

Thanks for taking a look — Redwood is assembling a small cross-vendor working group (we're calling it the "Storage Sherpa" council) to align on three practical things customers keep asking for: idempotent write semantics across vector stores, sync/replication contract expectations (hot vs cold tiers, TTL behaviors), and a lightweight partner playbook for fallthrough routing.

Proposed agenda (attached: StorageSherpa-Agenda.pdf):
- Quick intros (5m)
- Customer ask patterns and measurements (10m)
- Idempotency semantics: api-level guarantees and retry behavior (20m)
- Sync contracts: acceptable divergence windows and cold-tier handoffs (20m)
- Next steps: shared contract draft and test harness (10m)

Primary asks: please confirm an engineer or product contact who can speak to replication/consistency (we'd love someone who can share the top 2-3 gotchas from production) and confirm availability next week for a 60-minute sync.

Proposed times: Mon Nov 9 9:30–10:30 PT or Tue Nov 10 11:00–12:00 PT. If neither works, propose two alternate slots and we'll do our best to accommodate.

Link to shared notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1StorageSherpa/agenda-and-notes
Attachment stubs: StorageSherpa-Agenda.pdf, sync-contract-draft.md (draft placeholder)

Thanks — looking forward to getting a small kernel of folks together.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Partner Solutions (Redwood Inference)
avery.johnson@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Storage Sherpa: idempotency, sync contracts & partner playbook — invite

Adding a technical note from the Redwood runtime side so the discussion is grounded. Short version:
- Idempotency surface: we need a small, well-defined idempotency token (server-accepted) for writes that span multiple backends; the token should survive retries for a configurable window.
- Partial writes: common failure mode is multi-backend partial success (one vector persisted, another not). We recommend a canonical reconciliation endpoint (delta-report) that returns per-shard status and conflict hints.
- Cold-tier semantics: if we recommend S3-tier fallthrough, we must be explicit about expected read-latency and eventual consistency (e.g., index rebuild window) and how embeddings TTLs are enforced.

I'm attaching a draft we plan to bring: sync-contract-draft.md (API surface + test cases). If others can add 2–3 test cases they care about to the doc before Tue, we'll triage within the call.

Count Weaviate in as well. Appreciate the clear agenda — Tue Nov 10 11:00–12:00 PT works for me and we'll bring an engineer who owns the S3 spillover connector. A couple of quick notes to add to the agenda before the call:
- Cross-store index mapping: we should align on a minimal common metadata schema so that fallthrough lookups have deterministic keys (namespace, vector_id, version).
- Test harness: suggest a small reference suite (3 scenario seeds) that everyone can run in CI: (1) writer retries + partial failure; (2) re-index from S3 cold tier; (3) index divergence after a network partition.
